extraction_scope: Worker-6 source-reviewed mechanism-relevant claims from abstract, Results, Methods, figure captions, and Discussion; no figure-only exact numeric bar values were fabricated.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: CF-labeled HC-1(R) and [D]HC-1(R) were observed initially at bacterial membranes and later inside E. coli; [D]HC-3(R) appeared to enter rapidly, with no discernible gross inner-membrane disruption in the reported images.
direct_assay_types: confocal microscopy with CF-labeled peptides and FM4-64
mechanism_claims.limitations: Qualitative microscopy localization; exact membrane-disruption quantification is not reported as a table in local materials.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: In C. albicans, CF-labeled peptides localized on or around the membrane, then entered cells; PI uptake in dying cells supports intracellular translocation during killing.
direct_assay_types: confocal microscopy with CF-labeled peptides and propidium iodide
mechanism_claims.limitations: Qualitative microscopy evidence; mechanism after intracellular entry remains inferred by the authors.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: The authors interpret salt-resistant activity as consistent with electrostatic interaction with negatively charged microbial membranes rather than formation of bilayer-spanning pores.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: HBD-1/HBD-3 C-terminal analogs in this paper
mechanism_claims.limitations: Mechanistic model is author interpretation from salt/cation sensitivity and microscopy, not a direct pore-formation assay.

mechanism_cautions: No supplementary spreadsheet/table changes mechanism evidence; local supplementary .bin assets are PLOS landing/guideline/article HTML pages.
